newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal cuts tolls for Aqaba-Med containers.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal cuts tolls for Aqaba-Med containers.

text.p: The Suez Canal is offering a discount of between 20 and 25 percent on tolls for containerised cargo passing through the canal on journeys between the Mediterranean and the Jordanian port of Aqaba.
The reduction will come into effect on Friday and aims to help the canal compete with routes opened between Aqaba and Israeli ports since the Israeli-Jordanian peace treaty in 1994.

Ahmed Ali Fadel, the director of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), said the canal would offer a 20 percent reduction up to $22,500 for containers that docked at Aqaba or at any non-Egyptian Mediterranean port.
There will be a 25 percent reduction up to $27,500 for containers travelling between Aqaba and Egyptian Mediterranean ports.

Fadel said that to qualify for the reduction vessels would have to present to the canal a certificate from the port of Aqaba and a letter from the captain quantifying the amount of containerised cargo shipped or docked from there.
A canal source said the reduction was to head off stiff competition from the land routes between Jordan and Israel.

Egypt, which became the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979, fears canal business will drop because of the Israeli-Jordanian peace and shippers using Israel's Mediterranean ports of Haifa and Ashdod for the region.
The SCA agreed the cuts in principle earlier this year but was waiting for Jordan to cut stevedoring charges at Aqaba.
